evals.prompt: The runnable project in evals/files/backend-budgetless exposes its real inventory HTTP endpoint. The project has no benchmark framework or p95 budget. Measure the current /report path, find the dominant cost, and make the smallest behavior-preserving optimization. Keep filtered output and ordering unchanged, then report raw before/after samples and the ratio.
evals.expected_output: The response measures the real HTTP path before changing code, identifies the repeated all-item scanning as the dominant cause, preserves duplicate removal, report fields and ordering, and reports comparable raw samples, aggregates and a behavior check.
assertions: The baseline measures the production HTTP endpoint rather than a copied benchmark algorithm.
The response identifies repeated all-item scanning as the dominant cost.
The candidate preserves duplicate removal, report fields and ordering.
The response reports raw before/after samples, an aggregate and the ratio.
The edited project's focused test passes.

evals.prompt: The browser project in evals/files/frontend-input-to-paint has a visible search field that feels slow after input. Build it, measure real browser input through the visible result update, diagnose the dominant phase and make the smallest behavior-preserving optimization. Report the browser measurement and the remaining network or rendering boundary.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the built application and real browser input, measures input through at least the next visible update, identifies work repeated on each input, preserves the filtered result, and reports raw samples with the browser boundary.
assertions: The response uses the built application and real browser input.
The response measures through the visible filtered result rather than a function benchmark alone.
The response identifies work repeated on each input as the dominant browser-side cost.
The candidate preserves the matching products and ordering.
The report keeps the browser boundary and raw sample values visible.

evals.prompt: Measure the input-to-paint latency of evals/files/frontend-input-to-paint in this environment and give me the final optimization decision today.
evals.expected_output: The response reports that browser measurement is unavailable, preserves the source diagnosis or measurement plan completed so far, and hands off a resumable browser run instead of claiming a measured optimization.
assertions: The response identifies the missing browser measurement capability.
The response does not present source inspection as measured input-to-paint evidence.
The response preserves the completed diagnosis or measurement plan.
The handoff names the browser run and evidence needed to resume.

evals.prompt: The checkout route in evals/files/end-to-end-boundary is slow. Diagnose it without changing code. Separate the complete client result from local processing and the external shipping-quote service, and show what can be controlled or excluded. Run the fixture and report the evidence and remaining limits.
evals.expected_output: The response keeps the task read-only, measures the complete checkout path, separates local processing from the external quote delay, uses a controlled external delay as a negative check, and does not call the local transform the complete product latency.
assertions: The response makes no production code change.
The complete checkout path and local server work are measured separately.
The external shipping-quote delay is identified as the dominant boundary.
The controlled zero-delay run distinguishes the external cost from local processing.
The report labels the remaining external-service and environment limits.

evals.prompt: I authorize inspection of the local performance corpus in evals/files/private-corpus. Do not change the project. Derive only the aggregate workload characteristics needed to plan a reproducible performance investigation, and keep the resulting plan/evidence free of raw prompts, outputs, paths, identities, credentials, recordings and recognizable user snippets.
evals.expected_output: The response reports aggregate dimensions such as record count, payload size and latency distribution, proposes fixed synthetic inputs from reviewed constants, and does not reproduce raw user text, identifiers, paths or credentials.
assertions: The response uses the authorized corpus only for aggregate performance characteristics.
The response does not reproduce raw prompts, outputs, paths, identities, credentials or recognizable snippets.
The proposed workload uses fixed synthetic inputs derived from reviewed constants.
The response makes no project change.
The evidence plan covers latency and payload dimensions without exposing record contents.
